description: 12-month journey of a Tokyo restaurant opening. Single user planning, opening, and running a small Italian restaurant in Higashi-Azabu.

sessions.topic: Initial idea exploration - quitting corporate job, restaurant concept
key_facts: User name: Kenta Morishita, age 34
Quitting job at Marubeni Corporation after 11 years
Savings: 28 million yen
Initial restaurant name idea: 'Ginza Trattoria'
Target: small Italian restaurant, 20-25 seats
Inspiration: 2019 trip to Bologna, studied at Hotel School of Bologna for 3 weeks
Wife: Ayako Morishita, supports the plan

sessions.topic: Market research - studying Tokyo Italian restaurant scene
key_facts: Visited 14 Italian restaurants in 2 weeks
Benchmark restaurants: Ristorante Aso in Daikanyama, Faro in Ginza, Heinz Beck in Marunouchi
Average ticket size target: 8,500 yen per person dinner
Lunch target: 1,800 yen set
Identified gap: northern Italian (Emilia-Romagna) underrepresented

sessions.topic: Business plan draft - financials, breakeven analysis
key_facts: Projected monthly revenue at full capacity: 4.2 million yen
Breakeven: 38 covers per day average
Working with accountant: Hiroshi Tanabe of Tanabe & Partners
Tanabe office address: 2-7-3 Shibuya, Daiichi-Bunko Building 5F
Loan plan: Japan Finance Corporation, applying for 15 million yen at 1.85%
Scouted 23 properties via real estate broker Yusuke Hamada of Plaza Homes Commercial
Hamada cellphone introduced through college friend Daichi Sasaki
Areas considered: Nishi-Azabu, Higashi-Azabu, Hiroo, Yoyogi-Uehara, Kagurazaka
Ruled out Ginza due to rent (above 95,000 yen per tsubo)
Signed lease at 3-14-7 Higashi-Azabu, Minato-ku, 1st floor of Azabu Heights Building
Floor area: 64.5 square meters (about 19.5 tsubo)
Rent: 487,000 yen per month, plus 73,000 yen common area fee
Key money: 6 months rent (2,922,000 yen)
Lease term: 4 years renewable
Previous tenant: small French bistro that closed October 2024
Three quotes from contractors: Kenchiku Plus, Yamamoto Koumuten, Sasaki Design Build
Selected Yamamoto Koumuten led by Tetsuo Yamamoto
Yamamoto recommendation: use open kitchen with brick-faced pizza oven facing dining room
Renovation budget: 8.4 million yen
Yamamoto suggested supplier 'Forno Bravo Japan' for the wood-fired oven
Japan Finance Corporation approved 12 million yen (3 million below request) at 1.95%
Total opening capital secured: 36 million yen (28M savings + 12M loan minus expenses already incurred)
Decision to scale back interior finishing to compensate
Renovation started June 9, 2025, projected completion August 22
Floor: white oak engineered plank from Toyo Wood Works
Walls: limestone-finish plaster (Italian product Marmorino imported via Tokai Sangyo)
Bathroom layout changed at architect's suggestion: single accessible unisex instead of split
Wood-fired pizza oven ordered from Forno Bravo Japan: model 'Modena 100', cost 1.6 million yen
Pasta extruder: La Monferrina P3, cost 580,000 yen, sourced through Reizou Sangyo
Refrigeration: 2 Hoshizaki upright units, total 720,000 yen
Decided against rotisserie - too niche for menu

sessions.topic: Supplier sourcing - dry goods and produce
key_facts: Olive oil supplier: Solleone Japan, sourcing Frantoio Franci EVOO at 4,200 yen per 500ml
Flour: Caputo 00 imported through Suzuki Foods, 3,800 yen per 25kg sack
Produce: morning delivery from Tsukiji-Ota Market via broker Kenji Ueno of Ueno Seika
Ueno introduced through accountant Tanabe (Tanabe's wife runs catering)
Wine supplier: Nakata Shoji
Account manager: Mariko Nakata, daughter of company president
Mariko introduced by sommelier friend Reiko Igarashi from Hotel Okura
Initial cellar: 280 bottles across 47 labels, 60% Italian, 25% French, 15% Japanese
Opening cost for wine inventory: 1.85 million yen
Decision to rename from 'Ginza Trattoria' to 'Osteria Morishita'
Reason: 'Ginza Trattoria' confusing since restaurant is in Azabu
Logo designed by Aiko Fujimoto, freelance designer, fee 320,000 yen
Brand colors: terracotta and ivory
Domain registered: osteria-morishita.tokyo
Hired head chef: Marco Petrelli, 38 years old, Italian national from Modena
Petrelli previously sous chef at Ristorante Acqua Pazza in Daikanyama for 4 years
Salary: 720,000 yen monthly, 13-month bonus structure
Petrelli will start September 1, 2025
User found Petrelli through wine supplier Mariko Nakata's industry contacts
Renovation completed August 26 (4 days late)
Final renovation cost: 8.87 million yen (470,000 yen over budget)
Overage due to electrical panel upgrade required by inspection
Health permit inspector: Mr. Ogawa, Minato Ward Health Department
First inspection passed with two minor issues: handwashing signage and grease trap label

sessions.topic: Menu finalization with head chef Petrelli
key_facts: Final menu: 6 antipasti, 5 primi (3 pasta + 2 risotto), 4 secondi, 3 desserts
Signature dish: tagliatelle al ragu bolognese, hand-cut, 2,400 yen
Pizza: not on menu - oven used for focaccia and roasted secondi only
Lunch menu: 2 courses 1,800 yen, 3 courses 2,400 yen
Dinner average ticket projection revised down: 7,800 yen per person

sessions.topic: Sous chef and front of house hiring
key_facts: Sous chef hired: Haruki Nakajima, 29 years old, previously at Trattoria Goccia
Nakajima salary: 380,000 yen monthly
Service manager: Eiko Sawada, 41 years old, hotel background, salary 460,000 yen
Two part-time servers: Yui Tachibana (university student) and Naoki Hirose
Total staff at opening: 5 full-time, 2 part-time
Soft opening dates: October 8-11, 2025 (four days, dinner only)
Invited guests: 80 total, 20 per night, free meals with feedback forms
Guest list includes: investors, suppliers, food media (3 critics), neighborhood residents
Wine pairing offered but separately charged at cost
Petrelli running full kitchen brigade for first time

sessions.topic: Soft opening debrief - what went well and wrong
key_facts: Soft opening complete. Major issue: kitchen ticket times averaged 38 minutes (target 22)
Cause identified: pasta water station too small, bottleneck on plating
Positive: 73 of 80 guests rated meal 8/10 or higher
Food critic Akira Mochizuki from Tokyo Calendar published positive note on Instagram
Service manager Sawada flagged that table 7 has acoustic issue near AC vent

sessions.topic: Grand opening preparation and last fixes
key_facts: Grand opening date set: November 4, 2025
Pasta station expanded by adding second induction burner (cost 180,000 yen)
Table 7 acoustic issue fixed with felt panel installation
Press release distributed to: Hot Pepper Gourmet, Tabelog editorial, Tokyo Calendar, Nikkei Style, Foodie Tokyo
Reservation system: TableCheck, 32,000 yen monthly base + transaction fees
Grand opening November 4 went smoothly, fully booked
First three days: dinner covers 22, 26, 24 against target 28
Lunch service started November 5: 14, 18 covers (target 30)
Average ticket actual: dinner 8,100 yen (above projection), lunch 1,950 yen
First Tabelog rating after 3 reviews: 3.42
Part-time server Naoki Hirose quit after 2 weeks - found higher-paying job
Replacement: Sara Komatsu, 23, started November 17
Sous chef Nakajima reports back pain - reducing his hours temporarily
Considering hiring a dishwasher (currently servers double up)
Dishwasher candidate: Mrs. Yoneda, 58, lives in same building
November revenue: 3.42 million yen (target 4.0M)
Costs: food 31%, labor 38%, rent+utilities 18%, other 9%
Loss for month: 312,000 yen
Cash runway: roughly 14 months at current burn
Decision: change opening hours - cut Monday lunch, add late seating Friday/Saturday

sessions.topic: Holiday season prep and corporate booking
key_facts: Marubeni Corporation (user's old employer) booked December 22 private dinner: 24 guests, 12,000 yen per person fixed menu
Total December private bookings: 4 events, projected 1.1 million yen
Hired Mrs. Yoneda as dishwasher, 1,400 yen per hour, 4 hours nightly
Christmas menu launched: 5 courses 9,800 yen, optional pairing 4,500 yen
December revenue: 4.95 million yen (best month so far)
Holiday bookings exceeded plan by 38%
First year-end staff bonus distributed: 1 month salary equivalent for FT, 30,000 yen for PT
Petrelli requested 2-week vacation in February to visit family in Modena
Sawada proposed launching wine club membership in spring
January first week revenue down 42% versus December average
Implemented inventory system: changed from paper to Square Plus inventory module
Subscription: 18,000 yen monthly
Discovered 8% food waste, target reduction to 4%
Chef Petrelli adjusting menu: dropping branzino dish (low margin), adding guinea fowl

sessions.topic: Wine club design and member recruitment
key_facts: Wine club name: Cantina Morishita
Membership fee: 36,000 yen annual
Benefits: monthly tasting dinner, 10% off bottle list, first access to allocations
Target: 40 members by April
Sawada designed program; Mariko Nakata sourcing exclusive labels

sessions.topic: Petrelli vacation coverage and Nakajima promotion
key_facts: Petrelli on vacation February 14-28, 2026
Nakajima running kitchen during absence, given temporary 80,000 yen monthly bump
Hired part-time line cook for coverage: Toshiya Inoue, culinary school graduate
Menu simplified during coverage: dropped guinea fowl temporarily
Lunch service paused February 17-21 (extra precaution)

sessions.topic: Mid-coverage check-in and unexpected press visit
key_facts: Nakajima holding up well, dinner ticket times 24 minutes average
Tabelog rating climbed to 3.61 after 24 reviews
Unexpected visit by Hiroko Sano, restaurant critic from Asahi Shimbun Weekly
Sano did not announce herself but Sawada recognized her
Article publication expected late March

sessions.topic: Petrelli return and Q1 financial picture
key_facts: Petrelli returned March 1, brought back artisanal balsamic from family contact
New supplier added: Acetaia Giusti via Petrelli direct (saves 18% versus current import)
Q1 revenue total: 11.8 million yen versus plan 12.5 million
Wine club Cantina Morishita: 23 members signed, target 40 by April
Considering raising prices on 4 menu items
Sano review published March 19, 2026 in Asahi Shimbun Weekly
Headline: 'Azabu's Quiet Modena: A Trattoria With Conviction'
Review highlights: ragu bolognese, wine list, 'unfussy precision'
Reservation requests spiked 4x in 48 hours
Now booked 3 weeks out for Friday/Saturday dinner

sessions.topic: Menu price revision and supply chain adjustments
key_facts: Menu prices revised April 1: dinner average ticket target raised to 9,200 yen
Tagliatelle al ragu bolognese raised from 2,400 to 2,700 yen
Lunch courses raised: 2-course to 2,000 yen, 3-course to 2,600 yen
Olive oil switched from Frantoio Franci to a less expensive blend from Solleone (saving 22% on cost)
Customer feedback on price change: minimal pushback, no review impact
Wood-fired oven Modena 100 cracked on stone deck April 13
Emergency repair by Forno Bravo Japan technician Mr. Saito
Repair cost: 340,000 yen, 5-day downtime
Insurance through Tokio Marine Restaurant Plus policy covered 70% of repair
Adjusted menu temporarily: focaccia served as crostini, no oven-roasted secondi

sessions.topic: Six-month milestone and staff retention discussion
key_facts: Six-month anniversary approaching November 4 -> May 4
Service manager Sawada renegotiated to 510,000 yen monthly salary (raise of 50,000)
Petrelli bonus structure adjusted: 4% of revenue above 4.5M monthly threshold
Wine club Cantina Morishita reached 42 members (exceeded April target)
Considering second seating system for Friday/Saturday
Six-month anniversary May 4 marked with private gathering for 30 regulars
Customer database (via TableCheck) shows 412 unique guests, 87 repeat customers
Top repeat customer: Mr. Hiroyuki Tachibana (10 visits), Azabu resident
Revenue cumulative: 28.4 million yen since opening
Cumulative loss reduced to 1.1 million yen (was 1.8M at month 4)

sessions.topic: Considering second location and growth strategy
key_facts: Hamada (broker from Plaza Homes) showed property in Tomigaya, 18.2 tsubo, 580,000 yen rent
User cautious - one-year mark not reached yet
Petrelli interested in expansion as long as Modena focus preserved
Decision: revisit second location after fiscal year end September 2026
Instead: launch private dining room conversion in existing space

key_subjects: Convert storage area at rear into 8-seat private room
Cost estimate from Yamamoto Koumuten: 1.4 million yen
Loss of storage requires basement rental: 38,000 yen monthly nearby
Construction window: 4 weeks, scheduled July 14 to August 9
Marketing as 'Sala Modena' for private bookings, premium pricing
key_facts: Convert storage area at rear into 8-seat private room
Cost estimate from Yamamoto Koumuten: 1.4 million yen
Loss of storage requires basement rental: 38,000 yen monthly nearby
Construction window: 4 weeks, scheduled July 14 to August 9
Private room name: Sala Modena, premium pricing
Total staff now: 7 full-time, 4 part-time
Added social insurance enrollment for all FT (was previously voluntary)
Employee handbook drafted with help from labor consultant Mr. Endo, fee 280,000 yen
First formal performance reviews scheduled July 1
Discussed succession - if Petrelli ever leaves, Nakajima identified as successor
Performance reviews completed for 7 FT staff
Salary adjustments: Nakajima raised to 440,000 yen (from 380,000), Yui Tachibana raised to 1,500 yen per hour
Two-year retention bonus formalized: 200,000 yen at 24 months
Petrelli signed two-year extension to October 2027 with revised package
Petrelli new monthly base: 780,000 yen

sessions.topic: Private room construction and pre-opening marketing
key_facts: Sala Modena construction underway, on schedule
Pre-bookings already secured: 6 private events for September
Marubeni (former employer) booked Sala Modena October 14 for 14-person dinner
Pricing: 18,000 yen per person minimum plus venue fee 50,000 yen
Wine pairings start at 6,500 yen

sessions.topic: Reflection on year one journey and forward outlook
key_facts: Looking back to March 2025: from idea to thriving restaurant in ~17 months
Tabelog rating now 3.78 with 91 reviews
Cumulative loss zeroed out in July 2026, now operating profitably
Sala Modena opens August 12, 2026
Year-two goals: second location decision by November, possible cookbook collaboration
Final word: the user reaffirms the original mission - Modena-style cooking in Azabu
